title: DevSecOps, Pod Security, NetworkPolicies & Supply Chain
summary: Harden Kubernetes clusters with Pod Security Standards, Zero-Trust NetworkPolicies, Trivy vulnerability scanning, Falco runtime eBPF detection, and Kyverno policies.
learningObjectives: Isolate sensitive workloads using Kubernetes NetworkPolicy ingress/egress micro-segmentation.
Harden pod security contexts (`runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, read-only rootfs).
Audit container images with Trivy and runtime syscall integrity with Falco.

curriculumModules.title: Zero-Trust Micro-Segmentation with NetworkPolicies
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: By default, all Pods in a Kubernetes cluster can communicate with all other Pods across namespaces. A NetworkPolicy restricts L3/L4 traffic based on pod and namespace label selectors.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Apply a default-deny ingress/egress NetworkPolicy in every namespace and explicitly allowlist only required microservice-to-database paths.

curriculumModules.title: Pod Security Standards, Trivy & Falco Runtime Defense
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Defense-in-depth combines pre-deployment CVE scanning (`trivy`), admission control (`PodSecurity` restricted profile + `Kyverno`), and kernel eBPF syscall detection (`falco`).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce `runAsNonRoot: true`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`, and drop `ALL` Linux capabilities.

labs.title: Enforcing Zero-Trust NetworkPolicy Database Isolation
labs.scenario: Sensitive customer records live in `vault-db` in namespace `production`. Create a `NetworkPolicy` named `vault-db-netpol` selecting `app=vault-db` to enforce ingress micro-segmentation.
labs.productionContext: PCI-DSS and SOC2 audits require strict L3/L4 network segmentation around all database pods.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: vault-db-netpol
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vault-db
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Inspect `kubectl describe networkpolicy vault-db-netpol -n production` to confirm `spec.podSelector.matchLabels.app` is `vault-db`.

labs.title: Pod Security Hardening (Non-Root Execution & Trivy Image Scan)
labs.scenario: Scan `nginx:1.27-alpine` with `trivy` and harden deployment `token-signer` in `production` so its Pod `securityContext.runAsNonRoot` is set to `true`.
labs.productionContext: Running containers as root (UID 0) allows container-escape vulnerabilities to gain root privileges on the underlying Linux host.
objectives: Scan `nginx:1.27-alpine` for CVEs using `trivy image nginx:1.27-alpine`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: token-signer
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: token-signer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: token-signer
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: signer
          image: nginx:1.27-alpine

steps.title: Scan Container Image with Trivy
steps.instruction: Run `trivy image nginx:1.27-alpine` to verify zero critical CVEs.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl get deploy token-signer -n production -o json` to verify `spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot` is `true`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which Kubernetes Pod Security Standard profile enforces the strictest controls (non-root execution, dropped capabilities, seccomp profile required)?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The `Restricted` Pod Security Standard enforces current pod hardening best practices including `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, and dropping `ALL` capabilities.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the role of Falco in a cloud-native DevSecOps architecture?
options: Real-time runtime threat detection by monitoring Linux kernel syscalls via eBPF
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Falco is the CNCF runtime security project that inspects Linux kernel system calls via eBPF to detect abnormal behavior such as shell spawns inside containers or sensitive file reads.
